item.title: Kristin Cavallari makes steamy bedroom confession ahead of 40th birthday
item.description: Kristin Cavallari revealed intimate details about her sex life on her "Let's Be Honest" podcast as she looks ahead to her upcoming 40th birthday.
item.content:encoded:
Kristin Cavallari is giving fans an inside look at what goes on in her bedroom in a steamy confession on her podcast.

In a recent episode of her "Let's Be Honest" podcast, the 39-year-old reality star opened up about her upcoming 40th birthday and gave some insight into her sex life, noting she isn't having sex but says: "Your sex drive as you get older is like wild."

"Like age 40, I'm way more sexual than I was at 25. Again, it would be nice if I had an outlet for it, but we can have sex with ourselves, which is what I f---ing do all the time," she said. "But that's one of the reasons why I can't wait to be in a relationship is I feel like I've become this like sexual being."

She explained that her last relationship "was a very sexual relationship," but that that was something she needed, and admits it is something she misses.

KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION

Cavallari added that she is now looking forward to turning 40, saying, "If this is what 40s is, like f- - - yeah. This is fun."

Earlier in the episode, the "Very Cavallari" star quipped that it "takes one to two years of abstinence to become a nun" and that she is on her way towards that achievement.

The reality star was previously married to former professional football quarterback Jay Cutler from 2013 to 2020, when she announced they were getting a divorce. They share three children; Camden, 14, Jaxon, 12, and Saylor, 10.

When speaking about her divorce, on the "Aspire with Emma Grede" podcast in July 2026, the "Laguna Beach" star claimed she gained the confidence to leave her marriage because of the success of her company, Uncommon James.

But because I had this company, there was a really large asset on our balance sheet," she said. "I didn't get anything, which I'm so happy about now. But I don't get any money from my ex-husband. I had to give him half the value of Uncommon James in cash and properties and everything else. Yeah. Isn't that interesting?"

Following her divorce, she dated Mark Estes for a few months in 2024 and country singer Morgan Wallen. She told Bunnie XO on the "Dumb Blonde" podcast in December 2024 that Wallen "was good in bed."

"I'll be honest with you. He was the first guy in my f---ing life that wasn’t just completely enamored with me ... It really threw me," she said. "I love having the upper hand and I feel like with him, I didn't have the upper hand."

item.title: Indiana Hoosiers boost College Football Playoff hopes with 27-13 win over USC Trojans
item.description: Indiana's defense forced costly USC Trojans turnovers in the red zone as the Hoosiers moved to 9-1 and kept their playoff hopes firmly alive.
item.content:encoded:
The Indiana Hoosiers' hopes of making the College Football Playoff and defending their national title are still alive thanks to a 27-13 win over the USC Trojans.

It's kind of hard to believe that USC and Indiana had only played five times going into Saturday's game in Bloomington, and boy, was this one big.

Both teams came in facing what was effectively a "must-win" scenario as far as having a shot at the College Football Playoff.

CFP REACTION: ALABAMA FEELS THE LOVE, INDIANA GETS THE SHAFT AND BIG 12 GETS RELIEF AS COMMITTEE CONFUSES US

Lincoln Riley and the Trojans have struggled on the road, and that's what they were facing on Saturday. As for the Hoosiers, their ground game took a hit before the game even began when running back Turbo Richard was ruled out.

Both defenses were clicking in the first half, which put points at a premium. Indiana struck first when QB Grant Wilson hit tight end Brock Schott for six.

Somewhat strangely, both teams missed field goals in the first half, but each of them made up for it with another. That made it a 10-7 game with under a minute until halftime.

That's when USC's Deven Bryant picked off Wilson, putting the ball back in quarterback Jayden Maiava's hands.

After a 51-yard bomb to Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, Maiava hit wideout Zacharyus Williams for a 7-yard touchdown to tie it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Each team added a field goal early in the second half, and then Indiana pulled ahead thanks to a five-play, 75-yard drive, capped off by a Khobie Martin touchdown.

USC followed with a lengthy drive that ended early in the fourth quarter with a field goal attempt to cut the Indiana lead to four.

However, kicker Caden Chittenden — who came in after Ryon Sayeri missed a field goal on the first drive of the game — missed a kick of his own, costing the Trojans some much-needed points.

Later in the quarter, the Trojans found themselves deep in Hoosier territory, but once again, they left points on the board when Maiava threw an interception in the red zone.

It proved to be even costlier than that, as the Hoosiers took the ball 93 yards, most of it thanks to a 42-yard touchdown pass to Charlie Becker.

Those miscues for USC added up, and the final one came on 4th-and-13 at their own end of the field. Maiava — who, in fairness, was running out of options to keep his team in it — threw a prayer downfield, only for it to be picked off by defensive back Jamari Sharpe.

That was all she wrote. A third loss on the year means it's pretty much curtains for USC's playoff hopes, while Indiana moves to 9-1 on the year and 6-1 in Big Ten play.

The Hoosiers will head out to Washington next week to take on the Huskies, while USC will look to bounce back against the struggling Maryland Terrapins.

item.title: Robot dogs mounted with rifles deployed in anti-gang stadium operation in Haiti
item.description: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele shared video of armed robot dogs storming Sylvio Cator Stadium as forces joined Haitian police in a gang crackdown on the violent island nation.
item.content:encoded:
El Salvador President Nayib Bukele released a video this week showing military forces using robotic dogs mounted with rifles in an operation to take back a stadium in Haiti from gang control.

"Under the bilateral agreement between the Haitian government and the government of El Salvador, a joint operation involving the Haitian National Police, the Haitian Armed Forces (FAd’H), the Task Force, and the Salvadoran Special Forces successfully took control of Sylvio Cator Stadium and secured it," Bukele wrote on X in a translation from Haitian Creole.

The video showed the robots moving down a hallway and up a set of stairs with the rifle on top.

EL SALVADOR-BACKED AIR ASSAULT DESTROYS HAITI GANG HEADQUARTERS AMID SEARCH FOR MISSING TROOPS

It’s unclear exactly how the robots assisted in the Port-au-Prince operation.

Bukele said "several human skulls" were found inside the stadium during the operation.

'THEY FED HIM HIS OWN EARS': TOP REPUBLICAN SHARES HORRIFYING STORIES OF GANG RULE IN HAITI

"We will now establish an operational base at the stadium so we can continue advancing deeper into territory controlled by the gangs," he said. "We now have the upper hand on the ground."

Bukele demanded gang members leave the area before their offensive began.

JOHN KOUFOS: TRUMP’S ‘SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS’ COULD HELP DEFEND US FROM CARTELS

"Those who choose to stay and fight our forces will have to face the consequences," he said.

Cracking down on gangs has been a hallmark of Bukele’s presidency since he took office in 2019.

item.title: Millions of Americans use marijuana to sleep, but new study raises troubling questions
item.description: A Northwestern Medicine study found that marijuana users had objectively worse sleep quality, even though they didn't perceive their sleep as worse. Other experts weighed in.
item.content:encoded:
Marijuana may be making sleep quality worse, despite its widespread use as a sleep aid, a recent Northwestern Medicine study found.

The findings of the study, which included 1,266 participants, showed that both lifetime and recent cannabis users objectively had worse sleep quality, although they did not report their sleep to be worse.

Participants were monitored for almost 35 years, from young adulthood into middle age, with scientists tracking their use of cannabis over time.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

In middle age, participants wore a sleep monitor on their wrist for a week and filled out surveys about their sleep quality.

This allowed researchers to compare objective and subjective reports of participants’ sleep.

"Our data do not support the belief that cannabis is helpful as a sleep aid," said senior study author Mercedes R. Carnethon, Ph.D., as Northwestern Now reported.

"As cannabis becomes increasingly available and accepted, it's important to better understand its long-term associations with health behaviors such as sleep," Carnethon added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Among all participants, a greater lifetime exposure to marijuana was linked to worse objective sleep quality.

Those who had a higher cannabis usage over time were generally asleep for a lower percentage of the night and experienced more sleep disruption.

Similarly, recent cannabis users were more likely to have more sleep fragmentation and lower sleep efficiency, compared to people who never used the substance.

The study also found there was a much higher chance that recent cannabis users would sleep longer than eight hours per night. 

The study discusses the differences between objective and subjective reports of sleep quality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"What makes this study particularly interesting is that participants who used cannabis demonstrated objectively poorer sleep, yet their own assessments of sleep quality did not reflect those differences," Alfred Joshua, M.D., a board-certified emergency medicine physician based in California, told Fox News Digital. (He was not involved with the new study.)

"In other words, someone may believe marijuana is helping them sleep, while objective measurements suggest otherwise." 

Researchers considered multiple outside factors including age, race, sex, smoking frequency, alcohol consumption, physical activity and more.

Even with these factors taken into account, the study found a consistent correlation between cannabis use and poorer objectively measured sleep.

The mode of cannabis consumption, such as smoking versus taking edibles, was not considered.

"It is not surprising that the actual quality of sleep of these subjects, after chronic marijuana use, is poor compared to those who do not smoke marijuana because people who claim that they need to smoke marijuana before they go to sleep, in order to relax, are only kidding themselves," board-certified psychiatrist Carole Lieberman, M.D., of California told Fox News Digital. (She, too, was not affiliated with the new study.)

"It is more a psychological addiction than a physical one," she added. "They enjoy the high that they get right away, but the marijuana doesn't help them to sleep better."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The researchers found that greater cumulative cannabis exposure was associated with reduced sleep efficiency, increased sleep fragmentation and more time spent awake after initially falling asleep," said Joshua, the board-certified emergency medicine physician. 

"These findings raise important questions about whether habitual marijuana use is a sustainable strategy for managing sleep problems," he added. 

Fox News Digital recently reported on other cannabis findings.

A study of nearly 450,000 American adults, for instance, linked cannabis use to an increased risk of stroke and cardiovascular disease.

The findings were scheduled for presentation at the American Heart Association’s Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago Nov. 6–9. They showed that both casual and heavy marijuana users have higher odds of heart conditions compared to non-users.

Khloe Quill of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Private planes and roadtrips: AEW goes above and beyond to get to Phoenix for Full Gear despite travel chaos
item.description: Tony Khan dispatched private jets to hub locations to fly AEW talent to Phoenix after nationwide flight cancelations threatened Full Gear.
item.content:encoded:
All Elite Wrestling (AEW) dropkicked a nationwide nightmare to make sure its talent and personnel made it to Phoenix for Full Gear on Saturday despite travel chaos that plagued millions across the U.S.

AEW owner Tony Khan brought in some wrestlers and other workers on private planes just to make sure they were going to show up for the fans, who were expected to pack the Mortgage Matchup Center for one of the company’s top pay-per-views on the calendar.

"I know it’s been an incredibly challenging few days for a lot of people," Khan said in a video posted to his social media. "My sympathies to everybody affected by all of the flight cancelations and delays. Yesterday, as you can imagine, was a hectic day as it was for a lot of people with the flights grounded and that applied to all flights yesterday – private and public flights. For AEW, we’re the same as everyone else, we’re not trying to break any rules. Everybody was grounded and we started formulating a plan that has come together really, really well."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Khan said everyone on the Full Gear pay-per-view card arrived in Phoenix. Khan sent private planes at three "hub locations" to bring the wrestlers and other personnel to the Mortgage Matchup Center. The only thing that changed was the Tailgate Brawl – which will occur on the Full Gear pre-show.

Khan said he believed everyone probably would have made it on their scheduled flights.

"I think it was virtually impossible given how many flights of people who work in AEW have been canceled had I not dispatched the private planes to the three hub locations, I think it’s very unlikely everybody would have made it here. I think there probably would have been some changes to the main card."

Adam Copeland, who battles Kazuchika Okada for the AEW International Championship, said it was "challenging" to get from the East Coast all the way to Phoenix.

"I was going down the runway about to take off for Denver and the pilot came on and said there’s a ground stoppage nationwide. I was like, ‘OK.’ I called Beth (Phoenix) and she came and got me and I went home," he said. "No idea if I was going to make it today. All of my flights started getting canceled one after the other after the other. Everyone else’s flights were starting to take off but mine weren’t.

"Even still, my flight to get out here is tomorrow at 5:37. So, Tony Khan sent a plane to come get us. Poor (Tony) Schiavone got there early so he was sitting there at 9 o’clock. I don’t think we were taking off until 11 so I was like, come have a coffee, come pet my dogs. We had a big dog cuddle-fest this morning and my girls got to meet Tony and we had some coffee – we made the best of it."

Tony Schiavone, one-third of the AEW broadcast team, was set to fly out of Atlanta when he made the last-minute decision to take a smaller plane out of Asheville, North Carolina, because of the uncertainty that he may have been delayed or canceled. He told his wife he wasn’t going to drive all the way to Phoenix, but he would have if he had the time to make the 27-hour trip.

LIVE COVERAGE: THOUSANDS OF FLIGHTS CANCELED AFTER LONGEST NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP IN 25 YEARS ROCKS US AIRPORTS

"But that was OK because I waited, got to hang out with Adam Copeland, which was pretty cool," he said. "It was a pretty cool day but it was a very challenging day. I guess I got here around 2 o’clock local time here in the afternoon. My car is still in Asheville. I have no idea how I’m gonna get it but it doesn’t matter. I’m glad I’m here. I would do anything to make it to Full Gear. … I would have driven to Phoenix! I would have, but I didn’t have the time."

Mark Davis and Jake Doyle, the duo known as Davis and Doyle, will challenge for the AEW World Tag Team Championship against The Young Bucks. But it was far from easy for them to get to the arena.

"Tumultuous last 24 hours leading up to Full Gear," Davis said. "For me, I had to run across the great state of Florida. I went from Tampa to Orlando, trying to get a flight – didn’t happen. Thankfully, the big guy had our back and I think he’s pretty excited to see Davis and Doyle take down some Young Bucks here this evening at Full Gear."

Doyle made it clear, "It’s a bad day to be a Buck."

"It was already a bad day to be a Buck but then I had to drive to Detroit, then drive to Chicago, then sit on a private jet, which is pretty awesome, but I had to sit on that jet for eight hours, waiting to get here to tear up these Young Bucks.

"So, Tony Khan, thank you for that jet. Young Bucks, I don’t feel sorry for you."

Matt and Nick Jackson – The Young Bucks – were only in California. They had to make the drive to Phoenix.

"We told each other, we’re blessed, we’re in California. A lot of these guys are coming further than us, but we will do anything – planes, trains and automobiles – we will be here at Full Gear," Matt Jackson said. "We have a big match tonight – Davis and Doyle. Two intimidating meatheads that actually had our number the last couple times when we’ve been in the ring. We talked about it on the drive. We had six hours to really think about it and strategize. Yeah, the travel sucked but we’re ready and we’re gonna rock the house tonight at Full Gear."

Excalibur, Schiavone’s broadcast teammate, said he was at the gym when he got a text about the travel chaos. He said he planned to jump in a car to go from Southern California to Phoenix. He drove five hours to get to the arena but took solace in the fact he got a chance to stop in the desert he doesn’t normally stop in.

"I made it. I wouldn’t miss this for the world. I know people have much tougher travel days than I did. I mean a five-hour drive, it’s doable, but in wrestling terms, it’s nothing," he said. "I wasn’t going to miss this for the world. I know a lot of people in AEW, everybody in AEW, has the same idea, same feeling, if there’s any way possible for them to be here today, they’re gonna be here at Full Gear. … There’s nothing that can keep me from Full Gear today."

Nigel McGuinness, the third person on the broadcast team, got to Phoenix from Los Angeles. He jumped in his car when he learned about the travel woes.

"There was no way I was gonna miss Full Gear," he said. "There’s something about being in professional wrestling where you make the show no matter what. I’ve never missed a show and there was no way I was going to miss Full Gear."

The main pay-per-view card begins at 8 p.m. ET and can be seen on HBO Max.

item.title: Michigan loses again and the noise around Kyle Whittingham's job grows as Oregon keeps playoff hopes alive
item.description: The No. 16 Oregon Ducks defeated Michigan on Saturday, dropping the Wolverines to 5-5 as noise continues to grow around Kyle Whittingham's job.
item.content:encoded:
If you close your eyes and listen closely, you can hear the faint heartbeat of the Oregon Ducks' College Football Playoff hopes.

On the other hand, for Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham, the noise surrounding his job is deafening. No. 16 Oregon (7-3) beat Michigan (5-5) 31-7 on Saturday. The outlook for both teams couldn't be more different.

The loss for Michigan makes the possibility of Whittingham being a one-and-done head coach all the more real, while Oregon keeps it playoff hopes alive.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Ducks came out flying, scoring touchdowns on two of their first three possessions of the game. Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola opened the scoring when he connected with wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan on a deep ball for a 60-yard touchdown, putting Oregon up 7-0.

The Ducks' second touchdown of the opening quarter came with less excitement, but the points still counted the same. Raiola hit running back Da'Juan Riggs in the flat for his first career receiving touchdown to put Oregon up 14-0.

It looked like the Ducks were on their way to an easy win, but Michigan running back Savion Hiter got the Wolverines on the board with a 70-yard rushing touchdown to cut the deficit in half, making it 14-7.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Michigan looked like it was going to go into halftime down one score, but instead it had a complete coverage breakdown with seconds remaining in the first half. Raiola scrambled outside the pocket and connected with Dakorien Moore for a 59-yard touchdown after Moore got behind the defensive backs to put Oregon up 21-7.

Coming out of the half, Michigan benched quarterback Bryce Underwood for Tommy Carr, looking for a spark.

It looked like Michigan was going to cut into the deficit at the beginning of the fourth quarter, but the Oregon defense slammed the door with the Wolverines on the Ducks' 3-yard line, forcing a turnover on downs. With the game out of reach, Oregon tacked on another score with a 49-yard touchdown from Dierre Hill Jr. off a screen pass.

With just over four minutes left, Whittingham went back to Underwood to end the game.

Oregon's next game is against Michigan State, and beating the Spartans is paramount to staying alive in the playoff race.

For Michigan, its next two games are against ranked opponents. Next week, the Wolverines play No. 4 UCLA and then end their season against No. 20 Ohio State. Losses to either or both of those teams could spur changes in Ann Arbor.

item.title: Tennessee Volunteers overcome sluggish offense, jet lag to take down Texas A&M and keep CFP hopes alive
item.description: The Tennessee Volunteers overcame an FAA ground stop delay and a quarterback injury to beat the Texas A&M Aggies on the road to keep CFP hopes alive.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, the Tennessee Volunteers needed a fourth quarter explosion to put the Kentucky Wildcats away.

History repeated itself seven days later in College Station, as the Vols overcame a sluggish first half and a quarterback injury to vanquish Texas A&M on the road and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive.

Before we go any further, it's important we address the elephant in the room, and that is the FAA ground stop.

FAA GROUND STOP LIFTED ON FRIDAY NIGHT, BUT SOME COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS STILL SCRAMBLING TO TRAVEL

Although Tennessee coach Josh Heupel likely won't admit it, his team's late arrival in the Lone Star State may have contributed to their sleepy start on offense.

The Vols arrived at the team hotel just before 1 a.m. local time, likely offering an explanation for the lack of fireworks on offense.

Luckily for Heupel, his defense was up for the challenge, harassing Aggies quarterback Marcel Reed all afternoon to the tune of just 71 yards passing.

The Aggies could only muster one touchdown the entire game and were held to only 179 total yards.

UPDATED START TIMES FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAMES AFFECTED BY FAA GROUND STOP, BROKEN DOWN BY CONFERENCE

It's been a hard fall for Texas A&M, who began the season as a top-10 team before falling out of the AP top-25 entirely.

Saturday's loss has the Aggies in danger of missing a bowl game, and they still have a showdown with a surging Texas squad to end the season.

For the Vols, a letdown almost surely would have meant the end of their CFP aspirations, as a third loss could have put those dreams on life support.

Things looked bleak until, ironically, Tennessee was bit with the injury bug when starting quarterback George MacIntyre went out midway through the third quarter.

From that point, the Vols remembered they could run the ball and run it quite well at that, rushing for 196 yards on the day and holding the ball for over 42 minutes.

If Tennessee can replicate this formula of salty defense and controlling the time of possession, they will be a hard out in December and beyond.

With that in mind, the Vols have a date with the LSU Tigers next Saturday before a road game in Nashville against rival Vanderbilt.

If they can navigate that stretch undefeated, they will be a shoo-in to make the CFP.

Once they make it, I doubt anyone will want to play this version of Tennessee.

item.title: Kathy Ireland’s husband escapes burning boat after engine explodes 20 miles offshore
item.description: Kathy Ireland shared dramatic footage of husband Greg Olsen's boat engulfed in flames after an engine explosion 20 miles west of Santa Barbara.
item.content:encoded:
Kathy Ireland is thankful after her husband narrowly escaped a fire that engulfed his boat while he was alone at sea.

In a recent Instagram post, the 63-year-old actress shared video of husband Dr. Greg Olsen's boat, the 4th Watch, engulfed in flames. Ireland said Olsen was out alone on the water while she was away on business.

"Life is really hard and really beautiful. God is great," she wrote. "Engine exploded and a fire quickly melted all navigation equipment and survival raft!"

She then thanked everyone "who prayed and continue to pray" for her husband, as well as all "those who aided in the rescue," including "@towboatus_ventura and the entire community" for their quick response.

KATHY IRELAND REVEALS 'BIG RED FLAG' THAT EXPOSED ALLEGED $100M 'UNCONSCIONABLE' BETRAYAL

"Most of all, we thank our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ for this miracle of his survival," she added.

Ireland also shared a note she wrote to her husband following the incident, saying her "heart is both heavy and full" because she knows how much "love, sweat and life you poured into this vessel."

"This vessel brought so much joy and so many blessings to our family and countless others," she continued.

"My heart is heavy with yours. This is more than a boat, there are many implications. My heart is mostly full. Full because of the outpouring of love and support. Multitudes were praying for you! I’m so thankful to all who rushed to pray and come to your rescue."

"I’m so thankful God gifted you with a brilliant mind to navigate this disaster so seamlessly," she added. "I’m eternally thankful to Him for loving and rescuing you. Though the vessel is no more, the 4th Watch is forever. You named that boat so profoundly. He has so much ahead for you! I’m so proud of you."

Fans in the comments section shared well-wishes for Ireland and Olsen, with some recounting their own experiences with losing their belongings due to a fire.

"Unbelievable!!! I’m SO grateful your husband is ok," one fan wrote. "🙏 And having parents who lost their home in a fire I completely understand your sadness about the loss of the boat. "

"Oh my! I am so glad he is safe," another added. "The boat and gear is replaceable, but the emotions are real. So sorry!!!!" A third follower wrote, "So sorry to hear this, BUT, Thankful to God that he saved your Precious One!"

The TowBoatUS Ventura Instagram account also shared video of the fire and its aftermath, saying the company received a call about the fire around 3 p.m. on Wednesday afternoon, noting the vessel was "20 nautical miles west of Santa Barbara Harbor."

In its post, TowBoatUS Ventura credited Olsen for his quick thinking, noting that he "was prepared and did everything right." They wrote that he initially "attempted to extinguish the fire before ultimately activating his EPIRB and abandoning ship into a kayak."

"This was about as good an outcome as one could hope for in an otherwise serious emergency," the message read. "A well-prepared mariner, good samaritans nearby, and commercial vessels equipped and ready to respond made all the difference. It is a great reminder of the importance of preparedness, cooperation, and the maritime community looking out for one another."

"Life with you is an awesome adventure! Our secret to our lasting love is no secret at all. It’s God’s design. item.title: Kai Trump opens up about relationship with Tiger Woods, her mother's boyfriend: 'I love him so much'
item.description: Kai Trump revealed how Tiger Woods helps with her golf game, calling her mother Vanessa Trump's boyfriend "the best" in a Golfweek interview.
item.content:encoded:
Kai Trump is getting some pretty good golf advice.

The 19-year-old's freshman season at the University of Miami was halted last month after she was forced to undergo another wrist surgery. But surely, her source of information has dealt with his fair share of injuries.

That, of course, is Tiger Woods, who is dating Trump's mother, Vanessa. Vanessa is the ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Trump and the 15-time major champion hard-launched their relationship in March of last year.

"He's the best. I love him so much, and he's a great guy, and he helps me whenever I want," the president's granddaughter said to Golfweek.

Shortly after Woods was arrested on charges of DUI, Vanessa Trump showed support for her boyfriend.

"Love you," Vanessa Trump wrote over a picture of herself hugging Woods as the two appeared to relax on a hammock. The photo, posted to her Instagram Stories early Friday morning, was the same photo Woods shared on X when he first announced his relationship with her.

Tiger's son, Charlie, and Kai Trump played at a tournament together at the 2025 Junior Invitational.

KAI TRUMP RECALLS ‘A LOT OF CRYING’ WITH MOM VANESSA BEFORE COLLEGE AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE

After his highly publicized divorce from Elin Nordegren, Woods was linked to Olympic skier Lindsey Vonn in the 2010s. He was dating Erica Herman at the time he won the Masters in 2019, but they, too, had a very public breakup that included sexual harassment allegations and an NDA lawsuit filed by Herman.

Woods and Nordegren have appeared to be amicable in recent years, as they co-parent Charlie and Sam Woods. The two were recently together at Charlie's high school where he officially signed to play college golf at Florida State.

Woods has played in just 18 events since the start of the new decade, and his best finish in a major during that span is a tie for 38th at the 2020 Masters.

Tiger's return to the golf course remains to be determined — he has not played since the 2024 Open Championship. When he was arrested in March, he said he was "hoping to" play in April's Masters, but he ultimately missed the entire 2026 season.

As for Kai Trump, it's not yet known when she'll return to the golf course, either.

item.title: Fetterman warns there is no longer 'common ground' with far-left Democrats over Israel
item.description: Sen. John Fetterman says he no longer sees any common ground with the far left on Israel and calls his 2028 primary challenger Ahmed Moor "pro-Hamas."
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., told Fox News on Saturday that he no longer sees "any more common ground" with the far-left wing of his party over its stance on Israel.

During an appearance on "Saturday in America," Fetterman criticized efforts to replace Senate Democratic Leader Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., with Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., and called his new 2028 Democratic primary challenger "pro-Hamas."

"I have a strong, strong difference of opinion on Israel and the Jewish community overall now. I don't think there's going to be any more common ground," Fetterman told Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany.

FETTERMAN REVEALS WHAT IT WOULD TAKE FOR HIM TO LEAVE DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"Now I think if someone can't identify [that] Iran is an enemy, and that it's committed to destroying Israel and our nation as well, too — once again, this is the kind of individual that the Democratic Party elected," he added.

Following midterm elections that saw Democrats regain control of both the House and Senate, Schumer is facing a challenge to his leadership. Van Hollen announced his bid to replace Schumer on Thursday, with support from progressive lawmakers, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich.

DEMOCRATS TURN ON SCHUMER AFTER HISTORIC ELECTION WINS AS POTENTIAL CHALLENGER EMERGES

Fetterman said a Van Hollen victory would be troubling.

"It would be troubling if my caucus elects someone like Van Hollen, that has really made his name being very... hostile to Israel," Fetterman said when asked if a Van Hollen win would cross a "red line."

SCHUMER'S FORMER ALLY MOUNTS LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE AS DEMOCRATS FACE RARE INTERNAL POWER STRUGGLE

Fetterman said Van Hollen has made his name on strong "anti-Israel" views and also received attention after his high-profile trip to El Salvador to meet with Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran migrant deported by the Trump administration.

"Other than that, I can’t really think of what Van Hollen's known for, but he became like a progressive darling, but I don't see that he has a path to be leader, but overall it's possible because just last weekend I had a lot of people protesting, demanding that we vote against Schumer," Fetterman said.

BITTER FETTERMAN-EL-SAYED FEUD THREATENS TO COMPLICATE SCHUMER'S SENATE UNITY PUSH

"We have to find a way forward. After our massive wins, we immediately go back to fighting amongst ourselves. Can't we just, you know, take the win?" he added.

Fetterman also called for bipartisan cooperation on the national debt, artificial intelligence, Iran and Social Security, expressing hope that Democrats could work with the White House.

"My hope [is] that our party doesn't revert to our worst impulses. I am going to extend and just hope for bipartisan solutions and work with the White House if that's possible. That's where my votes will be," Fetterman said.

Fetterman also criticized Gaza-born Palestinian-American writer and activist Ahmed Moor, who announced a 2028 Democratic primary challenge against him earlier in the week.

FETTERMAN RECEIVES NO SUPPORT FOR RE-ELECTION FROM PENNSYLVANIA HOUSE DEMOCRATS: REPORT

"This is someone that is very proud, very proud, pro-Hamas, and there are parts of my Democratic base [that] find my views more troubling or offensive, my strong support of Israel versus his views," Fetterman said.

"I'm always going to support Israel. Iran knows that the Democratic Party, it's very unlikely they're [going to] hold the Iranian regime accountable. I think we deserve to have that conversation," he added.

FETTERMAN WINS PRAISE FOR 'GUTS' AFTER GOING TOE-TO-TOE WITH JON STEWART OVER ISRAEL SUPPORT

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Moor's campaign pushed back on Fetterman's remarks, saying the candidate "condemns violence against civilians by anyone" and accusing the Pennsylvania senator of failing to represent his constituents.

"Ahmed Moor is running on a platform of dignity, justice, and the rule of law. This includes ensuring that American tax dollars are spent in ways that benefit Americans, not on killing innocent people abroad. These views are in line with the majority of Pennsylvanians, who Fetterman has failed to accurately represent in Congress," the campaign said.

The campaign added that Moor supports "an arms embargo and targeted sanctions until Palestinians have equal rights," saying he would "fight antisemitism and anti-Palestinian racism with the same conviction."

Fox News Digital reached out to Van Hollen for comment.

item.title: Iowa State running back has massive 3 TD opening quarter, caps it off with Michael Jackson impression
item.description: Aiden Flora scored three first-quarter touchdowns and rushed for 216 yards as Iowa State routed the Cincinnati Bearcats 41-13 at Jack Trice Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
You're going to be hard-pressed to find a better first quarter than the one we got out of Iowa State running back Aiden Flora on Saturday against Cincinnati.

The Cyclones welcomed the Bearcats to Jack Trice Stadium, and it really didn't take long to get an idea of how this one was going to shake out.

Iowa State won big, 41-13, with their biggest statement coming in the first quarter.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After the Bearcats scored a touchdown on their opening possession, the Cyclones answered back with not one, not two, but three of their own.

All of them courtesy of Flora.

And if three touchdowns in under 15 minutes of game time aren't impressive enough, he does a very solid Michael Jackson impression as well.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I feel old.

item.title: Trump takes parting shot at DC golf course conditions one day before major overhaul begins
item.description: Trump shared photos of what he calls "Trash Island" on Truth Social, blasting U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes for slowing the East Potomac overhaul.
item.content:encoded:
A day before a D.C. golf course is set to close for a major overhaul under President Donald Trump, the president took one more chance to take a shot at its apparently poor conditions.

In May, the National Links Trust announced that the Trump administration will be giving East Potomac Golf Links, a public D.C. course, a "historic restoration."

The project has faced roadblocks, including U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes saying she would open a "formal inquiry" to investigate if attorneys for the Trump administration violated ethical boundaries during a legal dispute about the project.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Trump said the course, which he called "Trash Island," is the "worst" in the world, "but the Department of the Interior is going to make it into the Best Golf Course anywhere in the World."

"Unfortunately, Judge Ana Reyes doesn’t want us to quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course," Trump said in a Saturday Truth Social post.

Trump also said the conditions of the course are "very dangerous," adding pictures of what appears to be the course in poor shape.

"The Fairways are far too close together. When you walk down the corridors of Trash Island, you don’t hear the sound of the running Potomac, all you hear is the sound of people screaming, 'FORE!'," Trump wrote.

SPORTS WORLD REACTS TO THE SUDDEN PASSING OF LEGENDARY BROADCASTER DAN HICKS AT THE AGE OF 64

"In any event, we’re making progress, and hopefully the Judge will agree that the Dignity, Beauty, and Importance of Washington, D.C., will be greatly enhanced by this soon to be beautiful Project. Trash Island, after years of laughter and scorn, will evolve into something very special, something which the Judge will be able to take great pride in seeing! All over the World it will be acclaimed as being the Best Golf Course anywhere."

Trump said the course will have the potential to host major golf tournaments, including the U.S. Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup and the Presidents Cup, and D.C.-area residents will be able to play for half off.

The course, located along the Potomac River near the National Mall, will be redesigned by Tom Fazio. It sits on federally owned land at East Potomac Park and has been part of Washington's public golf scene for more than a century.

The redevelopment has also drawn scrutiny over tree removal at the site. Reyes recently temporarily halted additional tree cutting amid a legal challenge over work at the property.

Fox News' Amanda Macias and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Tom Arnold admits he hasn’t dated in nearly 10 years after calling people his age ‘disgusting’
item.description: Tom Arnold reveals he hasn't dated in nearly ten years but says his "My Crazy X-Wife" comedy tour changed his outlook on finding love.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Arnold shared he's ready to fall in love again after being single for close to a decade.

During a recent interview with Page Six, the 67-year-old actor and comedian went into a deep dive about his love life, telling the outlet that "it would be good to love somebody and be loved."

"I used to say, people are like, because I haven’t had a date for nine and a half years, ‘You should date someone your own age,’" he said. "And I’m like, ‘Dude, have you seen people my age? We are freaking disgusting.'"

He went on to say that since meeting many different women while on his "My Crazy X-Wife" comedy tour, he changed his tune, saying he has "learned there's a lot of funny, smart, sexy 60-something women" out there.

VALERIE BERTINELLI SAYS SHE’S ‘REALLY SCARED’ OF DATING, ISSUES WARNING ON 'VULNERABILITY'

The "True Lies" star has been married four times. His first marriage was to Roseanne Barr, from 1990 to 1994.

Barr recently defended Arnold in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter after Chuck Lorre claimed in his memoir, "Sitcom," that "Roseanne" writers were encouraged to put Arnold's name on scripts "as if Tom had written them." Arnold later denied these claims to Entertainment Weekly.

"Unbelievably — I don’t think you’ll hear me say this often — but Tom Arnold is telling the truth for once. Talk about the paradigm switch here," Barr said. "Tom Arnold is defending me. I have to thank him for that. That’s the first time he’s done something right by me in his f---ing life. Thanks, Tom."

In response to Barr defending him, Arnold wrote on social media, "Hell finally froze over today."

Following the breakdown of his marriage to Barr, Arnold was married to hair stylist Julie Lynn Champnella from 1995 to 1999, Shelby Roos from 2002 to 2008, and Ashley Groussman from 2009 to 2020.

During their 11-year-marriage, Arnold and Groussman welcomed two children together; Jax, 13, and Quinn, 10. The couple had been separated for a few years prior to the finalization of their divorce.

When speaking to Page Six, Arnold shared that he doesn't think women are necessarily looking to date a man "that used to have a lot of money and now has two little kids," but in the meantime, he is happy with his kids and his friends.

"I love my kids so much," he continued. "That’s a lot of love there. And my buddies. But I’ll be okay. You know, I’ve had four marriages."

item.title: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith becomes Big Ten's all-time leading receiver in just his third college season
item.description: Jeremiah Smith broke the Big Ten all-time receiving yards record in just three college seasons at Ohio State, surpassing Purdue's John Standeford.
item.content:encoded:
Jeremiah Smith's (likely) final college season might not result in another national title, but he is now in the record books.

In just his third college season, the Ohio State wide receiver became the all-time leading receiver in Big Ten history during the Buckeyes' 28-19 win over Northwestern.

Smith had 11 receptions for 117 yards and a score for the Buckeyes, who have free-fallen out of the College Football Playoff bracket. But with the performance, he surpassed Purdue’s John Standeford's Big Ten mark in the second quarter while remaining front and center in the Heisman debate.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Standeford had 3,788 receiving yards in his four seasons with the Boilermakers, but Smith now has 3,875.

Smith is one of just 11 players inside the top-50, and three inside the top-15, to spend less than four seasons in the conference.

He also tied Purdue's David Bell and Michigan's Braylon Edwards with his 17th 100-yard game.

Smith made a statement the second he set foot in Columbus, as he led the Big Ten in receiving yards and touchdowns as a freshman — and he has only gotten better.

Last year, he was an All-American and finished sixth in the Heisman vote. This season, his 15 touchdowns are tops in all the FBS, and he figures to be in the conversation to be the first pick in next year's NFL Draft.

UPDATED START TIMES FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAMES AFFECTED BY FAA GROUND STOP, BROKEN DOWN BY CONFERENCE

Smith also led the Big Ten in catches and yards last year.

Smith accounted for more than half of the passing yards backup quarterback Luke Frahey threw on Saturday (201 total), as Julian Sayin continues to deal with an injury.

He figures to be yet another receiving star out of Ohio State in recent years, joining Chris Olave, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Garrett Wilson, Emeka Egbuka, Carnell Tate and Marvin Harrison Jr.

item.title: Maher challenges Sarah Huckabee Sanders on 'socialism' as Arkansas governor defends free school breakfasts
item.description: Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders pushed back after Bill Maher asked why free school breakfasts count as socialism only when Democrats offer them.
item.content:encoded:
Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders credited her education agenda with helping her defy a sweeping blue wave in the 2026 midterms, defending free school breakfasts after Bill Maher questioned why such programs are labeled socialism only when Democrats offer them.

"We focused on issues over the last four years of things that really impacted the day-to-day life of the people that we were elected to serve," Sanders said during Friday’s episode of "Real Time."

"I made no secret coming in that education was going to be a top priority, and we have legitimately transformed education in the state of Arkansas."

GOV SANDERS REVEALS 'MAJOR BREAKTHROUGH' ON EDUCATION AS RED STATE POSITIONS ITSELF AS 'BLUEPRINT' FOR NATION

Sanders highlighted several measures Arkansas has taken to improve student learning outcomes, including deploying literacy coaches, expanding school choice, raising teacher pay and providing free breakfasts for public school students.

She described the breakfast program as a bipartisan effort to ensure children aren’t trying to learn on an empty stomach.

"But how come it’s only socialism when they do it?" Maher pressed, referring to Democrats.

Sanders drew a distinction between providing meals to schoolchildren and broader government giveaways.

BROOKE ROLLINS, DR. BEN CARSON: WE ARE PUTTING REAL FOOD BACK ON SCHOOL LUNCH TRAYS

"There’s a big difference between giving everything away for free and helping kids start out on the right foot," she said.

"I don’t know that I would say those are the same thing."

Maher clarified that he supported Huckabee Sanders’ initiative.

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital, "Maher’s question exposes the game pretty cleanly. When Democrats use government to help people, Republicans call it socialism. When Sarah Huckabee Sanders uses government to give every public-school kid free breakfast, it becomes common sense." 

He added, "What Sanders really proved is that voters are a lot less interested in abstract fights about ‘big government’ than politicians pretend. If government is doing something visible that makes their lives better, they may reward it." 

The Arkansas Republican's broader discussion with Maher also focused on her longstanding support for President Donald Trump, with Maher questioning whether her loyalty to the president sometimes conflicts with her own principles.

"It seems like you are policy-wise you diverge from him, but you will never say a bad word or leave any daylight between you and what he does, which is very often different than what you do as governor," Maher said.

SARAH HUCKABEE SANDERS ACCUSES 'THE VIEW' HOST OF TWISTING HER WORDS IN IMMIGRATION EXCHANGE

Sanders rebuked any suggestion that she has a "blind loyalty" to the president, stating that many of her policies align with Trump's, but she also disagrees with him on some issues.

"I certainly support and appreciate a president who gave me an opportunity," Sanders said.

"Does that mean I agree with everything? No. Does that mean I think he does everything right? No. Neither do I."

Sanders, who has served as Arkansas' governor since 2023, won by 15 points over her Democratic opponent Fred Love earlier this month, overcoming the blue wave that largely swept the U.S. – even in traditionally red or toss-up areas like South Carolina, Mississippi, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Georgia.

item.title: At least 100 people pulled from Mississippi River after New Orleans ship crash as lengthy salvage effort looms
item.description: Officials say roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River after the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the docked American Heritage cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River after a tanker struck a docked cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday, officials revealed Saturday, as the U.S. Coast Guard prepares for a potentially weeks-long operation to remove the capsized vessel.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said 191 passengers and crew members were aboard the American Heritage when the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the vessel near the Port of New Orleans.

Everyone survived, though eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six patients were stable, officials said.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel from the American Heritage before salvage operations begin. Divers were expected to assess the vessel, while pollution response teams monitored the river for potential leaks.

NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY

Burnham said crews had not observed any product in the river requiring removal but warned that hazardous materials could potentially escape during the operation.

"As the mayor said, we're talking weeks, we're not talking days, we're talking weeks. So we're going to do this safely, and we're going to make sure that it's done right," Burnham said.

Moreno also revealed that the American Heritage's captain was injured but remained aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave the vessel.

"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

The captain initially refused medical treatment until he knew where everyone was, according to the mayor.

Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montro said responders evacuated more than 80 people before the vessel overturned, while roughly 100 people ended up in the river.

Montro said she estimated the American Heritage capsized within 30 to 45 minutes of the collision, though the exact timeline remains under investigation.

Officials credited life jackets and the rapid response of emergency crews and nearby vessels with preventing fatalities.

Investigators are examining a possible steering issue involving the tanker, though the exact cause of the collision remains unknown.

"I can say though I do not have any indication that this is terrorism related in any way, shape or form, but again, the investigators will continue to keep working through that," Burnham said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) confirmed Saturday that investigators recovered the Atlantic Asphalt's voyage data recorder, which captures information including the vessel's speed, course and audio from its bridge.

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said during a news conference Saturday that investigators will also examine the tanker's maintenance records and mechanical history as they work to determine what caused the collision. 

He cautioned that the agency remains in the early stages of gathering evidence and has not reached any conclusions.

DeLeeuw and a team of NTSB investigators began arriving Saturday after travel disruptions delayed its response.

DeLeeuw said 16 investigators were on scene and preparing to interview crew members and others involved. 

The agency said it expects to release a preliminary report in about 30 days, with a final report identifying probable causes and potential safety recommendations expected in 18 to 24 months.

The collision occurred around 12:30 p.m. local time Friday, when the tanker struck the American Heritage, which had been docked for approximately two hours. 

The vessel began taking on water before capsizing.

The Atlantic Asphalt has since been moved from the collision site, while the Coast Guard has partially reopened the river to two-way traffic. A 500-foot safety zone remains in place around the wreck.

American Cruise Lines, which operates American Heritage, is coordinating with local officials to assist displaced passengers as the investigation and recovery efforts continue.

item.title: Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit apologize for picking SMU over Wake Forest on College GameDay
item.description: Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit posted a humbling apology video after picking the SMU Mustangs, who found themselves trailing Wake Forrest 42-0 at halftime.
item.content:encoded:
What happened to SMU in north Texas was not just a beatdown. It was a shellacking of epic propositions by Wake Forest.

Wake Forest, the 13th-ranked team in the country, entered its road matchup against unranked SMU as a 2.5-point underdog and proved the oddsmakers just as wrong as College GameDay hosts Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit.

The two picked the surging SMU Mustangs during the College GameDay broadcast at Boise State, which featured Ian Johnson, the former Broncos running back who scored the game-winning two-point conversion against Oklahoma in the 2007 Fiesta Bowl.

WEEK 9 AP TOP 25 POLL MAKES A MOCKERY OF WAKE FOREST AND A LAUGHABLE OVERREACTION TO USC'S WIN OVER BUCKEYES

Fast-forward to halftime — SMU was down 42-0. The game wasn't close from the get-go, so McAfee and Herbstreit took to social media to provide a little humor and humility for their poor pick.

"We apologize to Wake [Forest]. Wake is real," McAfee said as Herbstreit put his arm around his colleague.

ESPN RIPPED BY FANS FOR HORRIFIC 'COLLEGE GAMEDAY' DECISION: 'RUINED THE SHOW!'

"I don't know what we were thinking," McAfee added as Herbstreit agreed.

"Boy, were we wrong," Herbstreit said with a sense of astonishment.

In my opinion, it wasn't an awful pick. SMU has a high-powered offense that put up 51 on Virginia Tech last week, but as they acknowledged in the apology video, Wake Forest has looked great too. The Demon Deacons have averaged over 50 points over the last three games.

Picking winners each week is not easy, unless you’re Steve Young, who went perfect as the guest picker when College GameDay visited BYU this season. But sometimes, when you’re wrong, you’re really wrong.

Wake Forest went on to win 49-7. So much for that prolific SMU offense.

item.title: 5 restaurant chains serving some of the best BBQ brisket in America, from New York to Oklahoma
item.description: From Mission BBQ to Dinosaur Bar-B-Que, these top barbecue chains serve up tender, slow-smoked beef brisket worth traveling for across America. Check out the list of winners.
item.content:encoded:
Brisket is an integral part of the menu at many barbecue joints, with one Texas restaurant recently sparking controversy after removing the cut of meat due to skyrocketing beef prices.

Americans eat about 58.5 pounds of beef per year as of 2025, according to the USDA — and diners seem to crave the tender, juicy cut that is brisket, which comes from the breast or lower chest of a cow.

AMERICA'S BEST FOOD CITIES RANKED BY EXPERT, WITH CHOICES THAT COULD INFURIATE LOCALS

The Takeout recently compiled a list of the best barbecue places in America to get brisket, citing smoking techniques, meat tenderness, flavor and customer satisfaction.

Here are five of the best barbecue restaurant chains in the country to get brisket — from New York to Oklahoma.

Since opening its doors on the tenth anniversary of the Sept. 11th terrorist attacks, Mission BBQ has been "proudly serving those who serve."

Dining rooms are filled with patriotic tributes to those who have served and protected the United States, and guests who drop in for lunch might catch the restaurant’s "daily salute to the Stars and Stripes," the chain’s website states.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Oak-smoked, tender brisket is served sliced or chopped on a sandwich, alongside other meaty classics like pulled pork or pulled chicken sandwiches, baby back ribs, smoked chicken and sausage, of which there are both jalapeño cheese and classic varieties. 

Kids or those with smaller appetites can enjoy mini brisket sliders.

At its many locations across 24 states, Mission BBQ aims to provide authentic barbecue made with fresh ingredients — the website even notes the restaurants do not have freezers or microwaves.

After developing a love for brisket while traveling through Texas, John Rivers founded 4 Rivers Smokehouse, with the first location opening in Winter Park, Florida, in 2009.

The chain wet-ages its brisket for 30 days, then massages it with a spice rub before it's smoked for 18 hours.

"Great brisket can't be rushed. It's a labor of love that takes patience, passion and a dedication to getting it right every single day," 4 Rivers Smokehouse told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"At 4 Rivers, brisket is more than a menu item. It's part of who we are, and we're incredibly proud to share that tradition with our guests," they added.

Aside from enjoying sliced brisket on its own or in a sandwich, diners can also order a brisket bowl or add the meat to the specialty Smoke Stack burger.

Created in 1983 as a concession stand to serve bikers at the Harley Rendezvous motorcycle gathering in Albany, New York, Dinosaur Bar-B-Que was the brainchild of John Stage and two partners — one of them named Dino, the company’s website states. Today, Dinosaur Bar-B-Que has locations in five cities in New York.

For its brisket, the chain uses USDA Prime beef that is aged for 30 days, smoked fresh daily over regional oak and hickory woods, then hand-sliced.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

A menu disclaimer says that, due to the "low and slow" daily smoking process, restaurants may run out of fresh smoked meats.

Guests can enjoy the brisket on its own or in sandwiches, combo plates and more. Additional menu items include pork belly sliders, a shareable shrimp boil, fried green tomatoes and a barbecue chopped salad.

Billy Sims, the 1978 Heisman Trophy winner and a former NFL running back for the Detroit Lions, worked with his business partner Jeff Jackson to open the first Billy Sims BBQ location in Tulsa, Oklahoma in 2004.

The chain now has over 30 restaurants across six states, with a menu featuring brisket that’s smoked slowly over pecan wood and served in a variety of ways, including chopped, sliced, in sandwiches and tacos, and more.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Guests can also opt for a brisket plate which comes loaded with two side dishes, Texas toast, pickles, onions and barbecue sauce.

If a plate’s not enough, brisket and other meats can be purchased by the pound.

Since opening in 1968 in Gainesville, Florida, Sonny’s BBQ has expanded to operate across eight states, and the chain takes barbecue seriously.

Those hoping to work as a pit master at Sonny’s must successfully complete the restaurant’s "P.I.T. Academy" education and training program, according to the website.

Brisket is smoked in-house each day, and it can be eaten on sandwiches, added to salads, or used as a topping on tater tots.

"The smoked wings, brisket, and baby back ribs were all moist and tender—just perfect," said a customer in a review on Yelp.

item.title: 'Dallas’ star Patrick Duffy says mother was killed rushing to husband after gunmen opened fire at bar
item.description: Patrick Duffy described how his father took a step toward the returning gunmen before they opened fire, killing both parents in their Montana bar.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Duffy's mother was doing a crossword puzzle when two armed men returned to the bar she and her husband owned in Montana, and one of them shot her husband. Moments later, she rushed toward him and was shot and killed, too.

The "Dallas" star, 77, recalled the final moments of his parents' lives during an appearance on the "Still Here Hollywood" podcast, revealing how the double murder unfolded and how he found the strength to carry on.

The murders took place nearly 40 years ago, on Nov. 18, 1986.

'DALLAS' STAR PATRICK DUFFY AND LINDA PURL RECALL START OF SURPRISING LOVE STORY: 'BOTH NERVOUS AS TEENAGERS'

"My parents were murdered when two young men robbed the bar that my parents owned in Montana," the actor told host Steve Kmetko. "My dad had thrown these two boys out because they were drunk and obstreperous. He just threw them out of the bar, and they went somewhere, finished whatever they were drinking, and the anger boiled up and they went back in."

Sean A. Wentz and Kenneth A. Miller were both 19 at the time, People magazine reported. Duffy's parents, Marie and Terence, were the only ones in the bar when the gunmen returned.

"It was very late at night," Duffy said. "There was nobody in the bar except my father and my mother, and they walked in with their shotguns. As soon as my dad saw them, this is in the testimony that came out in the court, my dad turned to them and apparently took a step towards them, saying, 'I told you to ...'"

WATCH: PATRICK DUFFY AND LINDA PURL FELL IN LOVE ONLINE

Duffy's father never finished his sentence.

"... That's when they opened up on him and killed him," Duffy said. "And then my mother was on the other end of the bar doing a crossword puzzle and took a couple steps running towards dad. And they shot her too."

"And then, if that wasn't stupid enough, instead of just running, they jumped over the bar to the cash register, took the money and a couple of bottles of booze and then left."

The Los Angeles Times previously reported that Terence and Marie's bodies were found by a group of people who had stopped for a drink after finishing their shifts at the nearby Montana Developmental Center. One woman spotted Marie on the floor but initially thought she might have fainted. When she saw blood on Terence, she went outside and flagged down a friend for help.

Duffy learned of his parents' deaths the following morning.

"... My sister had called she was completely devastated," he recalled. "... She was a police woman, and she was on her way to Montana. By the time I hung up the phone, there were film crews at the gate."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Duffy said Lorimar Television, the production company behind "Dallas," arranged transportation and other support for him following the murders.

"Lorimar [Television] called, everybody called, [the] support team got in there and said, 'We have the jet ready. We'll fly you to Montana. We'll take care of everything. We'll send a PR person with you to take care of all that.'"

Duffy said his Buddhist faith helped him cope with the loss. It also gave him the strength to tell his sons, Padraic and Conor, that their grandparents had been killed.

"The Buddhist philosophy is one of the continuous life cycle of your entity," Duffy explained on the podcast.

item.title: Democrats push back across the nation after voters approve girls' sports protections
item.description: Proposition 318 and similar transgender school sports bans passed in four states, but Democratic leaders in Washington and Colorado push back.
item.content:encoded:
The battle over girls' sports is moving from ballot boxes to courtrooms as the years-long national debate has gotten a new wrinkle this month.

Democrats are turning Election Day victories for the "save women's sports" movement into fresh fights to reject the will of American voters.

Voters in four states approved measures restricting transgender participation in school sports this month, but Democratic leaders in Washington and Colorado are either backing court challenges or considering changes to what voters passed.

JACKSON THOMPSON: WASHINGTON STATE DEMOCRATIC PARTY CALLS GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE UNCONSTITUTIONAL

The results highlight a divide between approval at the ballot box and acceptance among political leaders, even as some officials and athletic administrators commit to following the new laws.

Washington’s Initiative 638 passed with roughly 56% support. It prohibits biological males from competing in female school sports and requires students seeking to participate in girls’ athletics to provide healthcare documentation verifying their sex.

The Washington State Democratic Party quickly made clear that it supported continued resistance.

"The fight over I-638 is just beginning," the party said in a Nov. 6 statement.

The party argued the initiative violates the constitution and endorsed organizations planning court challenges.

The ACLU of Washington, Legal Voice and Pacifica Law Group subsequently sued on behalf of the state teachers union, a nonprofit and parents. The lawsuit argues that the measure discriminates against transgender girls and imposes unequal privacy burdens on girls seeking to play school sports.

The challengers seek to prevent the initiative from taking effect Dec. 3.

Seattle’s school board separately authorized legal action over the measure, citing concerns about privacy, equal treatment and conflicts with existing protections. That authorization allows the district to pursue legal action; it does not itself suspend the initiative.

Democratic Attorney General Nick Brown, meanwhile, appointed outside law firm Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend the law on the state’s behalf.

"My personal views do not dictate what laws get defended or the strength of that defense," Brown said.

ADF SEEKS TO DEFEND WASHINGTON GIRLS' SPORTS MEASURE, ARGUES STATE CANNOT FULLY REPRESENT FEMALE ATHLETES

Brown said the arrangement would ensure the initiative receives a defense while allowing his office to continue its other work protecting transgender rights.

Alliance Defending Freedom filed a motion on behalf of Female Athletes United to defend Washington’s voter-approved girls sports initiative against an ACLU-backed lawsuit, arguing that the state cannot adequately represent the athletes’ interests, on Friday.

The Nov. 13 motion asks King County Superior Court to allow Female Athletes United to join the case as a defendant to defend Initiative 638. The request seeks the court’s permission to participate; it is not an order granting intervention.

In Colorado, voters approved Proposition 134 with approximately 52% support, requiring school and college sports teams to be designated male, female or coeducational and generally tying participation to biological sex.

Democratic Gov.-elect Phil Weiser has already signaled an interest in changing the measure.

"We’re going to have to take a look at these anti-trans measures and what adjustments are necessary and appropriate," Weiser said after the election, according to reporting by The Colorado Sun published by Colorado Public Radio.

Weiser raised concerns about potentially invasive eligibility verification. The measure does not expressly require genital examinations or establish a uniform statewide verification process.

He had not outlined specific changes in the reporting reviewed. Because Proposition 134 changes state law rather than the constitution, lawmakers can amend it without another statewide vote.

Demonstrators in Denver have demanded repeal. Supporters, including Protect Kids Colorado, have accused Weiser of disregarding the electorate’s decision.

Colorado’s athletic administrators have taken a more direct position on compliance.

"Like every member school, CHSAA must comply with the new law," a Colorado High School Activities Association spokesperson told Colorado Public Radio.

Denver Public Schools also said it would support students while following state law. The measure is scheduled to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

Arizona voters approved Proposition 318 with approximately 59% support, expanding an existing law restricting male participation in girls’ sports.

The legislature referred the measure to voters with Republican support and Democratic opposition. Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs had vetoed similar legislation in previous years.

The proposition also restricts access to bathrooms, locker rooms and other private spaces based on sex recorded on an original birth certificate. It removes an existing provision allowing girls to participate on boys’ teams.

A pre-election lawsuit challenged the proposal, but a judge rejected the argument that it violated the single-subject rule and allowed it to remain on the ballot.

Opposition continued after passage. The ACLU of Arizona condemned the result, arguing that the measure further excludes transgender students.

"Lawmakers showed they would rather villainize vulnerable groups than defend our rights when they sent bad policies to the ballot, and unfortunately, some of those measures passed." said Victoria López, executive director for the ACLU of Arizona. "Proposition 317 will do nothing to make border communities safer, and risks labeling U.S. citizens and people seeking asylum as ‘terrorist organizations,’ Proposition 318 broadens an existing ban targeting trans student athletes to further ostracize kids who simply want to participate alongside their peers."

That statement did not announce a new lawsuit against Proposition 318. The absence of an announced post-election Democratic effort to block it should not be confused with an endorsement by Democrats who opposed it.

Nebraska’s Initiative 442 received roughly 68% support, placing restrictions on male participation in female school and college sports into the state constitution.

A voter guide published by the Nebraska Democratic Party recommended voting against it.

The proposal also survived a pre-election legal challenge. The Nebraska Supreme Court ruled Oct. 16 that the petition’s statement of purpose satisfied state requirements, rejecting an effort to keep the measure off the ballot.

The ACLU of Nebraska criticized the result after passage and said it would monitor potential harassment and discrimination against students. Its statement did not announce a new lawsuit.

Unlike Colorado’s statutory measure, Nebraska’s constitutional amendment cannot be undone through an ordinary legislative amendment. It reinforces a sports restriction already established in state law.

item.title: Bruce Buffer recalls wildest UFC brawls in and out of octagon, has strong words for banned Dillon Danis
item.description: Bruce Buffer recalls the Khabib Nurmagomedov and Conor McGregor cage brawl and shares his take on the Merab Dvalishvili hotel ambush in Abu Dhabi.
item.content:encoded:
Mixed martial artists are generally not friendly inside or outside of the octagon.

Brawls between fighters away from their fights are hardly a foreign concept, and there was another one in Abu Dhabi last week.

Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili was jumped by MMA free agent Usman Nurmagomedov, the younger brother of Dvalishvili's former opponent, Umar Nurmagomedov, in a hotel lobby overseas. Usman Nurmagomedov and his crew were sentenced to six months in prison.

Bruce Buffer has been the ring announcer since 1996, so he's seen his fair share of scary moments.

"I was at the Khabib [Nurmagomedov] and Conor McGregor fight when Khabib jumped over the cage. That was a big deal. I’ve also seen other brawls break out. I’ve seen so many; I’ve been doing this for 31 years," Buffer recalled in a recent interview with OutKick. (Ironically, Khabib Nurmagomedov is Usman and Umar's cousin.)

UFC will head to Madison Square Garden on Saturday, and the last time MSG hosted fights, Dillon Dannis got into a brawl with several of lightweight champion Islam Makhachev's team in the stands. That event got him banned from UFC, which Buffer is more than fine with.

UFC RING ANNOUNCER BRUCE BUFFER, 69, HAS NO PLANS OF RETIREMENT ANY TIME SOON; WANTS 'TO KEEP GOING'

"Dylan’s banned. Dylan should be banned. It seems every time Dylan goes somewhere, he causes trouble, so there’s no reason for him to be anywhere near us. I have no problem saying that," Buffer said.

Buffer then remembers another brawl that had occurred after UFC 13 in 1997.

"I remember a big brawl in the early days at an after-party. I was talking to Tank Abbott, and all of a sudden I saw Tank get hit across the face with an overhand right. It was Wallid Ismail, and all hell broke loose," Buffer said.

"When I’m in a brawl like that, I get my back to a wall so you only have to worry about who’s in front of you. Everybody’s going at it. Always keep your back protected and know where your exit is. Know where your six is. Just watch. But things happen."

Buffer said he was "sorry to see" that Dvalishvili got fined, "because it wasn't his fault."

"But those are the laws over there. Don’t do anything - don’t throw punches unless you’re in the ring or the Octagon," he said. "If you’re in Abu Dhabi, it’s not going to be a good outcome."
