item.title: Boise State head coach provides a refreshing, faith-filled College GameDay interview
item.description: Spencer Danielson's faith-focused responses on ESPN College GameDay in Boise Idaho ignited the crowd and drew massive praise from fans online.
item.content:encoded:
It's been 16 years since ESPN's College GameDay made its way to Boise, Idaho. Since the Broncos joined the FBS in 1996, they are in the top five for most wins with Ohio State, Alabama, Georgia, and Oklahoma. They have the most well-known playing surface in the sport: The iconic blue field. They are a Group of 6 powerhouse with the nation's leading rusher in Dylan Riley. Today, just like they did 16 years ago when College GameDay came to town, Boise State plays Oregon State.

College GameDay is always a lively, electric atmosphere, where the host team usually has their head coach speak with the panel of Pat McAfee, Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard and legendary coach Nick Saban during the broadcast. Saturday morning was no different.

Broncos Head Coach Spencer Danielson, who played linebacker and later coached for the then Division II Christian college out of Southern California, Azusa Pacific University, joined the panel, turning heads not only with his age (38) and positivity, but his faith-focused responses.

THE NFL IS AMERICA'S MOST GOD-CENTERED PROFESSIONAL SPORTS LEAGUE AND SUNDAY'S GAMES CONTINUED TO PROVE IT

In front of a sea of Boise State blue and orange, Danielson proclaimed as he answered Rece Davis's initial question, "First off, I appreciate all of you guys being here. And for me, man, always, thank you Jesus. We serve a God who's faithful."

As he said this, the crowd erupted.

Danielson wrapped up prefacing his answer by saying, "With God, all things are possible."

This echoed what Danielson said on Friday when he joined the "The Pat McAfee Show":

"I thank Jesus for the opportunity to be here because I’m not that smart, I’m not that cool. The only reason I’m the head coach is because Jesus put me here."

40 DAYS FOR LIFE CEO SHAWN CARNEY ON 'COLLEGE GAMEDAY' RELIGIOUS SIGN BAN: 'NOBODY'S FOR THIS'

In case you weren't aware of Coach Danielson and the way he conducts himself in interviews, this is nothing new. Many interviews start with a thankfulness to and praising of Jesus.

After securing their third straight Mountain West Championship in 2025, Danielson told Robert Griffin III, "First off, always, thank you Jesus. Faith doesn’t make things easy. It makes it possible. With God, all things are possible."

His statements on College GameDay received praise from many college football fans online.

"In the era of Godlessness we need more people like Coach Danielson," one X user said.

"Another reason I love Boise St."

"Spencer Danielson does this in every interview. Pay attention. Something extraordinary continues to happen in sports."

Danielson added in his interview with the College GameDay panel, "The only reason I'm here is Jesus."

He also said, "I know I'm here by [God's] grace and I wanna have an impact on these kids."

When you watch the game on Saturday evening, you'll hear much of the same from Coach Danielson.

item.title: Kentucky coach Mark Pope gives insanely tone-deaf answer after Wildcats nearly lose as 30-point favorites
item.description: Mark Pope told Rupp Arena fans he hopes they "had fun" after Kentucky needed a near-miracle to escape Northern Arizona 78-77 as 30-point favorites.
item.content:encoded:
With all the upheaval caused by the FAA ground stop on Friday evening, it's easy to forget there were plenty of intriguing sporting events taking place to provide an appetizer to a weekend of great football.

For example, college basketball is now in full swing and one game between a perennial power and a winless mid-major gave everyone a surprisingly drama-filled ending.

The Kentucky Wildcats are one of the bluest bloods in the sport, but their season was already off to a shaky start coming into Friday's matchup with the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks.

Big Blue Nation has already had to endure a scare against James Madison and a 20-point beatdown at the hands of the Kansas Jayhawks, but nothing could have prepared these Wildcat fans for what was to come in Rupp Arena against an 0-3 NAU squad.

My buddy Dan Zaksheske wrote an entire piece about the game itself, so check that out if you're interested, but suffice to say, Kentucky needed a near-miracle to escape against the visiting Lumberjacks.

What's worse, the Wildcats were 30-point favorites against Northern Arizona; this was supposed to be a "get right" game.

Instead, Kentucky needed a couple of front-end misses from a pair of one-and-one opportunities at the free throw line from its opponent and some Rupp magic to squeak out a 78-77 "victory."

COLLEGE BASKETBALL PLAYER'S BIZARRE FOUL SHOT GOES VIRAL IN SEASON-OPENER: 'DIABOLICAL'

It hardly felt like a win to all the fans in attendance, and just as the loyal folks of Big Blue Nation were trying to make sense of what just happened, the most tone-deaf man in America was giving a postgame news conference.

"I hope everyone in Rupp had fun."

IS IT WEIRD FOR A COACH TO NOT TALK TO HIS TEAM AFTER A GAME, OR IS IT EXTREMELY WEIRD?

Are you insane?

For context, that man is Mark Pope, head basketball coach for the University of Kentucky.

If you thought maybe that was the Northern Arizona coach, you would be forgiven, because in no world should a coach at a royally blue-blooded program like Kentucky ever say something like that after his $20 million roster just got worked by a mid-major.

He's lucky they didn't fire him right after the presser was over.

KENTUCKY COACH WILL STEIN TELLS WILDCATS PLAYERS 'IF YOU DON'T BELIEVE IN WHAT WE'RE DOING, YOU ARE HIGH'

"It's really entertaining," he said, without a hint of irony. "I think this will be a fun team to follow."

Yeah, for Tennessee, Florida, Arkansas, and Louisville fans, maybe.

But do you really think Wildcat supporters sat in the stands in Lexington last night and thought, "Man, I'm having a great time watching my eight-time national championship-winning program need a miracle to avoid what might be the worst loss in school history?"

Naturally, Pope got cooked over an open flame for this answer by both Kentucky fans and rivals alike.

I know I've been tough on Pope before, but stuff like this makes him hard to defend.

Kentucky fans were ready to get rid of John Calipari every season he failed to make the Sweet 16 towards the end there. I imagine those days feel halcyon by comparison.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After Pope's eventful spring, in which he lost out on top recruit Tyran Stokes and had a disastrous Q&A on social media, I suggested he lie low for a bit and do some soul-searching while the fanbase cooled down.

Not only did he not do that, he just turned the temperature up even higher on his already flaming-hot seat.

I don't envy anyone who decides to be the head coach at Kentucky. That place is a pressure cooker and a thankless job at that.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

But Pope is doing himself no favors by being this tone-deaf.

Either hire a PR team or start winning some tournament games, Mark, because this isn't going to get any better as it stands right now.
